castor.s01: 5 working days is how long it takes LOS to move money today. SC1 wants 1.
castor.s02: Thirty minutes in meeting room B4-12 — the whole project starts here.
castor.s04: CASTOR is item 7 of 9 on the Corporate Investment Board agenda. It gets eleven minutes.
castor.s05: Three options in the Business Case, and only one recommended. €8.4 m is the price of the one they pick.
castor.s07: 212 requirements gathered in six workshops — and none of them belong in the Project Charter.
castor.s09: The RfP gate checklist: 28 questions the Project Steering Committee must answer before Planning can start.
castor.s10: The Planning Kick-off. Twenty-one people, one room, 09:30 to 12:30 — the only time they are all together.
castor.s15: Twelve of a possible twenty-five on the risk grid: likelihood 3 × impact 4. Yellow, above appetite.
castor.s17: Seven work packages on the whiteboard — the Work Breakdown Structure, and everything under it.
castor.s18: 3,100 person-days priced across seven work packages, defended line by line.
castor.s19: Three weeks of procurement lead time wasted because the plan named the wrong approver.
castor.s20: Forty minutes to explain an outsourcing decision that was already made in March.
castor.s21: The contract runs two years before anyone signs an acceptance certificate.
castor.s22: Nineteen acceptance checks in the plan, and one contract clause that has to carry them.
castor.s23: Two systems running the same disbursement calendar for four months — the parallel run.
castor.s25: Forty loan administrators, and a benefit nobody can measure until 2029.
castor.s26: Four planning artefacts, four different approvers — and the surprise about who approves the Outsourcing Plan.
castor.s29: The Stakeholders Checklist is 90% complete. One row says 'partially', and that row is the whole scene.
castor.s33: Earned value: 90 cents of work delivered for every euro spent.
castor.s34: One page for the Corporate Investment Board — everything else is annex.
castor.s37: Likelihood 4 × impact 5 = 20. Red. R-07 has moved.
castor.s38: 4 Oct 2027, 16:40. R-07 stops being a risk and becomes issue I-14.
castor.s40: One version of the truth — and a document naming convention that enforces it.
castor.s43: 28 of 40 loan administrators trained with the go-live date fixed.
castor.s44: 998 of 1,000 migrated loans reconcile. The other two are why acceptance is partial.
castor.s49: 2029 is when the benefits appear — and the project no longer exists to be credited.

pollux.s01: 5 working days and 4 analysts per quarter-end — and then the requirement changes again.
pollux.s03: The Business Case and the Project Charter. Two documents PM²-Agile does not touch.
pollux.s04: The same 28 questions as the RfP gate in CASTOR. Agile does not delete the gate.
pollux.s05: Twelve principles taped to the wall. Characters quote them by line number.
pollux.s06: One Project Handbook, plus a Development Handbook inside it. Two books, one binder.
pollux.s08: Three iterations of enabler work before any business value ships — Einstein's argument, and Curie's answer.
pollux.s09: 8 Jan 2029 — the day iteration 1 begins, agreed at the RfE gate.
pollux.s10: Four hours of Release Planning, nine working days into the release.
pollux.s11: 09:30, standing, fifteen minutes. What the Daily Stand-up is, and what it is not.
pollux.s13: Explain the work first, estimate it after — why the order matters in Planning Poker.
pollux.s17: Two hours with the door shut: the Iteration Retrospective, and why stakeholders are not in it.
pollux.s18: The burn-down line stops falling on day 4. Nobody says so for six more days.
pollux.s19: Ninety minutes from the alert to the rollback. What a real incident looks like inside an iteration.
pollux.s20: Nine of eleven work items accepted in the Iteration Review. The other two are not failures.
pollux.s21: The same four logs as CASTOR — Risk, Issue, Decision, Change — plus the agile ones.
pollux.s24: Twenty-six retrospectives, and one Lessons Learned entry. Both are needed, for different readers.
pollux.s25: Eleven working days becomes one. The success criterion, finally measured.
